newPatternCandidates: brief-capability-mismatch-at-freeze (US-61, rw-16a5df77-L101): the frozen brief's acceptance needs file operations (delete/rename) that the worker wrapper's tools or the brief's write boundary cannot do. The worker finds this only after dispatch, and the cost was a full worker+verifier spend (~12k) with zero product change. Proposed fix: at plan-freeze, a preflight maps each acceptance criterion to the file operations it needs (create/edit/delete/rename/move) and checks them against the wrapper's allowed tools and the brief's write boundary. Any mismatch is a planning error, raised before launch.

blocked-routed-as-fix-retest: a worker block caused by missing scope or permission, with no code defect, lands in fixRetestQueue next to real verifier FAILs. This invites a same-brief re-dispatch that will block the same way, which is a runaway in the main session that the engine's halt cannot see. Proposed fix: the engine tags fix-retest entries with cause (verifier-defect vs worker-blocked-scope), and the main session must re-scope (PM/owner) before re-dispatching any worker-blocked-scope entry.

verifier-on-pre-write-block: the verifier runs a full pass (3593 tokens here) on an iteration where the worker reports it blocked before any write. It still fails to attest workspace integrity, so the main session must do a manual integrity check anyway. Candidate engine change: when the worker blocks before any write, run a cheap, deterministic integrity probe (tree-clean check against the batch base) in place of the full verifier, and route the result straight to recovery.
